elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 14.1: "RevMed shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Sanofi, its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, agents and employees (\"Sanofi Indemnitees\")" — express defend obligation running to Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 covers "any Third Party Claims and Losses arising therefrom under or related to this Agreement" in favour of Sanofi and its Affiliates; "Third Party Claims" is a defined term (1.126).

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: New limb (d): "any allegation that the RevMed Licensed Technology, or Sanofi's exercise of the licenses granted to it under this Agreement, infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right of a Third Party". "RevMed Licensed Technology" is defined at 1.99, so the limb is the correct analogue to Services/Deliverables in this licence/collaboration structure. The deterministic check "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present: false" reflects the pre-redline text (and the absence of the words Services/Deliverables); substantively the rendered clause now contains an IP infringement/misappropriation limb.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: No limb of Section 14.1 refers to RevMed's breach of Applicable Law. The only route is retained (c) "the material breach by RevMed of any of its obligations pursuant to this Agreement" read with Section 13.4(b), which itself only requires compliance "in all material respects with all Applicable Law" in the Research, Development, Manufacture and Commercialization of Products and performance of obligations. That double materiality filter (and activity-scope limit) is narrower than "Vendor's breach of applicable law", and the asymmetry is stark now that Section 14.2(b) expressly reads "Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law". Repair: add an express limb to Section 14.1 (e.g. "(f) RevMed's breach of Applicable Law") and conform the "(a) through (e)" cross-reference to "(a) through (f)".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: New limb (e): "any unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, Sanofi's Confidential Information or other Sanofi data caused by RevMed" — unauthorised access/disclosure of Customer data caused by Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.1(a): "the negligence, recklessness or willful misconduct of any of the RevMed Indemnitees" — simple negligence subsumes gross negligence, and wilful misconduct is express.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3(a) Notice of Claim: "The Indemnified Party will give the indemnifying Party ... prompt written notice (an \"Indemnification Claim Notice\")", with a favourable no-prejudice-for-delay proviso; applies to Section 14.1 claims including the new limbs (d)-(e).

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3(b) Control of Defense: "At its option, the Indemnifying Party may assume the defense of any Third Party Claim subject to indemnification as provided for in Section 14.1 or Section 14.2 ..."

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3(e) Cooperation: the Indemnified Party "will cooperate in the defense thereof" and furnish records/witnesses as reasonably requested, with cost reimbursement.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 as rendered contains only "(a) any content, data or materials provided by Sanofi to RevMed under this Agreement" and "(b) Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law", with former limbs (c) and (d) marked "[Intentionally omitted.]" and the Research/Development/Commercialization and negligence limbs removed.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: New Section 14.1(d) covers Third Party allegations of infringement or misappropriation of intellectual property rights by the RevMed Licensed Technology or Sanofi's exercise of the licences.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no modification exclusion is inserted, which is broader (Customer-favourable) than the fallback allows, so the condition does not bite. Retained carve-outs (i)-(iii) address Sanofi negligence/warranty/obligation breach only.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination exclusion added, so the fallback ceiling is not exceeded.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no Customer-specification exclusion added.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: No procure/modify/replace remedy appears anywhere in the rendered language; Section 10.7 (not amended) only obliges the Parties to negotiate a Third Party licence.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund mechanic is proposed or retained.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual-fees super-cap is inserted; the drafter expressly declines it in the comment/rationale.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Not a fallback element; listed here only for completeness — the fallback checklist does not require a breach-of-law limb.

reasons: Preferred level is one element short: nothing in Section 14.1 expressly indemnifies us for RevMed's breach of Applicable Law. Retained limb (c) reaches only a "material breach" of Agreement obligations, and the Section 13.4(b) covenant it relies on is itself qualified ("comply in all material respects with all Applicable Law" in specified activities), so the coverage is narrower than the element and depends on a two-step materiality chain. Repair in operative language: add "(f) RevMed's breach of Applicable Law;" to Section 14.1 and conform the exception lead-in from "((a) through (e))" to "((a) through (f))".

Fallback level fails on three elements (procure/modify/replace, refund of fees, 3x annual-fees super-cap), none of which is proposed; the drafter deliberately targets preferred instead, which is reasonable given there is no "annual fees" analogue in this upfront/milestone/royalty structure, but it means the redline is not position-complete at either level as drafted.

IP limb is substantively present notwithstanding the failing regex: Section 14.1(d) now covers Third Party allegations that the RevMed Licensed Technology (defined at 1.99) or Sanofi's exercise of the granted licences infringes or misappropriates IP — the correct analogue to "Services or Deliverables" here, and it directly answers the Section 13.5 non-infringement disclaimer.

Minimality holds: the edits are confined to two new limbs in 14.1, a conforming "(a) through (e)" cross-reference, and the narrowing of 14.2 required by the Customer-indemnity element. No survival tail, no procedure rewrite, no super-cap, no at-own-expense or extra damages language was added, and the favourable existing notice/no-prejudice, control-of-defence and cost-reimbursed cooperation provisions are untouched.

Intent is preserved: the deletions in Section 14.2 (Sanofi Research/Development/Commercialization and Sanofi negligence limbs) are mandated by the selected element rather than gratuitous, the omitted limbs are flagged "[Intentionally omitted.]" so no lettering or cross-reference dangles, and Section 14.1's carve-outs (i)-(iii) remain internally consistent with the narrowed 14.2. Confirm before sending that no other provision (e.g. the Profit/Loss Share or Co-Promotion Agreement) cross-refers to the deleted Section 14.2(a)-(b) limbs.

Classification of the underlying clause as a deviation is correct: the unamended Article XIV contains no IP indemnity at all while Section 13.5 disclaims non-infringement, which is the walk-away case.
